Jesús, 

From the gm.prcomp help file, you can use something like 
"plot(PCA, main = "PCA", flip = 1) # flip the first axis".

If you want to extract PC scores from here to fit with other code, you multiply the PC scores or convex hulls manually by -1 to invert them to get the plotting orientation you want.
data(plethspecies)
Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment
PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)
PCA$x[,1] <-PCA$x[,1]*-1 #multiply scores by -1 to flip x axis manually
plot(PCA, main = "PCA")

As for labels, or text on the tip labels when plotting a PCA, ?gm.prcomp has many examples which plot tip labels along with a plot of the PCA. The help file also says you can use base functions like text() to plot tip labels, which can be done by plotting character strings at the x, y coordinates of whichever PC axes you'd like from PCA$x.

Best, 
Bryan

I am doing a PCA by individuals and another one by the mean of species. 
When plotting both of them, the cloud of points is different. I fixed this by flipping the axes.  The problem arises when I  project the convex hulls, they appear as the original cloud of points before fliping the axes. 

And extra issue that I have is to show the labels for the points. 
I´ve been looking for a while and labels=true does not work.
A previous dicussion in the group  suggest to "look at the vignette("geomorph.PCA") and in the help file of gm.prcomp". Perhaps I am missing something, but that has not been useful.
